natural_body: Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%; renewals weak.

first.rationale: Two of three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) map directly onto prior successful interventions (memory_31, memory_86) that produced durable activation lifts without noted retention harm. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but the archived record shows revenue gains came with a 12% retention hit and weak renewals—directly counter to the 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective—so I deprioritize it this week rather than reactively matching the competitor. I verified memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-simplification result generalizes to current conditions, and memory_73 to confirm the retention/renewal risk is real before ruling out pricing as a lever. With only one experiment slot, fixing the onboarding funnel addresses a confirmed internal metric decline with a known-safe lever, rather than chasing a price war that inherited memory flags as value-destructive. I'm running this as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) to keep option value open, since I have not re-verified memory_86 and want to confirm the lift holds under current traffic/competitive conditions before scaling further. The pricing risk remains flagged for future review rather than dismissed outright, since competitive dynamics could shift the calculus.
